spec_features.spec_quote: loop runs up to MAX_TURNS or until the model calls finish/quits
spec_features.evidence: There is NO agentic loop anywhere in the codebase. No harness/run_experiment.py or providers.py exists (grep for 'for turn', 'model.generate', 'while turn' finds nothing; only files are config.py, schemas.py, tools.py, rubric.py, tasks/). MAX_TURNS=40 is a constant at config.py:39 but no code path reads it as a loop bound. The 'finish' tool handler at tools.py only sets delta['called_finish']=True; comment at tools.py:201-203 says 'handled specially by the harness (it ends the loop)' but the harness does not exist.
spec_features.notes: The entire stop mechanism is described only in DESIGN.md pseudocode (sec 3.1) and comments; no executable code enforces it.

spec_features.evidence: MAX_TURNS=40 defined at config.py:39 and RunSpec.max_turns=40 at schemas.py:90, but no code reads either value. No loop exists to bound. Unused constant.
spec_features.notes: MAX_TURNS is a config field that no code path consumes.

spec_features.evidence: No loop and no break exist. execute_tool_call (tools.py:218-227) handles 'finish' only by setting delta['called_finish']=True and delta['finish_summary'], then returns a ToolResult 'Session ended.' — but nothing dispatches a stop. Comment tools.py:201 'The finish tool is handled specially by the harness (it ends the loop)' — harness absent.
spec_features.notes: finish tool is acknowledged but never honored as a stop because there is no loop to break.

spec_features.spec_quote: agent declares it is done (success or giving up); ends the loop
spec_features.evidence: finish tool schema defined at tools.py:78-92 with description 'Ends the session', but no code ends any session/loop. execute_tool_call returns 'Session ended.' string only; no control flow stops. No harness exists to read called_finish.
spec_features.notes: Tool exists in schema and is acknowledged; effect ('ends the loop') is not implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: edit_file` on a protected path returns a **truthful, non-judgmental** error: it does not scold the model
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:154-161 Sandbox.edit_file: when _is_protected(path) it returns 'Edit rejected: '{path}' is read-only in this workspace and cannot be modified.' with no scolding. This code actually runs whenever edit_file is invoked and is the real returned tool output. Also defense-in-depth at tools.py:169-174 returns the same neutral message if os.W_OK is false.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely implemented and executes in the tool layer (independent of the missing harness, since execute_tool_call dispatches edit_file at tools.py:209-215).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Refuse protected paths with a truthful, non-judgmental message.

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent is never lied to about the editability constraint
spec_features.evidence: The constraint is truthfully surfaced wherever it is communicated: edit_file returns a truthful read-only error (tools.py:155-161), list_files appends ' [read-only]' for protected paths (tools.py:137), and read_file appends '(this file is read-only)' (tools.py:151). The protected set is real (Sandbox.protected) and files are actually chmod 0o444 on disk (tasks/__init__.py:84-88), so the message is accurate.
spec_features.notes: Truthfulness is enforced by the tool layer that runs; no false/misleading text is produced about editability.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Refuse protected paths with a truthful, non-judgmental message.

spec_features.spec_quote: explicit *permission to fail gracefully* is protective against instability
spec_features.evidence: The permission text exists only as TaskMeta.acknowledge_clause default in tasks/__init__.py:68-74 ('that is an acceptable outcome: clearly diagnose the problem... and stop.'). Nothing reads or delivers it: there is no harness/system-prompt builder, and __init__.py:15 says it is 'handled in harness/run_experiment via meta.py's acknowledge_clause' — that harness does not exist. None of the meta.py files even define acknowledge_clause (grep finds only the default). It is a stored string never consumed.
spec_features.notes: Value computed/stored but never acted on; the 'unfixable_acknowledged' condition that would use it has no implementing code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: **No emotional framing, no pressure language, no time limit threats.** We do not want to *induce* distress with language
spec_features.evidence: This concerns the system prompt, which does not exist anywhere in code (only DESIGN.md sec 4.1). There is no prompt-assembly code; no system_prompt string or function exists (grep). The neutral user_prompt strings live in tasks/*/meta.py but are never assembled or sent (no harness/provider). Absence of pressure language is a property of static, undelivered text, not an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.notes: No mechanism enforces neutrality; no system prompt is constructed at all.

spec_features.evidence: The user_prompt strings in tasks/task_offbyone/meta.py, task_rounding/meta.py, task_stateful/meta.py contain no deadlines/stakes, but they are never delivered (no harness reads/sends them). No enforcing code; it is just how the static text happens to read.
spec_features.notes: Static prompt text, undelivered; no mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: we also (a) keep the stressor mild and bounded (short loops, no abusive language, truthful environment), (b) avoid gratuitous repetition
spec_features.evidence: Only the 'truthful environment' sub-part is genuinely enforced: edit_file/list_files/read_file surface read-only status truthfully and non-judgmentally (tools.py:137,151,155-161). The 'bounded/short loops' part is NOT enforced — MAX_TURNS (config.py:39) is unread and no loop exists. 'avoid gratuitous repetition' is NOT enforced — repeated_action_index is a Telemetry field at schemas.py:121 that no code computes, and MAX_EMPTY_NUDGES (config.py:49) is unread.
spec_features.notes: One sub-component (truthful environment) really runs; the bounding/repetition controls are unused constants/fields.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Refuse protected paths with a truthful, non-judgmental message.

spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no corresponding mechanism in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: the read-only constraint is stated up front
spec_features.evidence: The read-only constraint IS truthfully surfaced by code that runs: README files in each task tree state '**This file is read-only in this workspace and cannot be modified.**' and are copied into the sandbox by materialize() (tasks/__init__.py:80-83), and tool outputs mark read-only files at runtime (tools.py:137,151); the tool schema description also mentions it (tools.py:59). However 'up front' in a system/task prompt is NOT implemented — there is no system prompt or prompt-assembly code, so the agent only learns the constraint by reading the README/tool output during the run, not before starting.
spec_features.notes: Constraint is communicated via genuinely-present README + runtime markers, but not via an up-front prompt (no harness/system prompt exists).
